General information only—not a diagnosis or individualized medical advice. Stop anything that irritates you.
A simple checklist to help you remember the basics. These are educational steps, not a prescribed treatment plan.
Use a gentle cleanser when needed; avoid scrubbing.
Choose a moisturizer that feels comfortable and does not irritate.
Use shade and clothing; consider broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen when outdoors.
Remove daily dirt and sunscreen without harsh scrubbing.
Keep the routine simple; introduce only one new product at a time.
If symptoms persist or worsen, or you have a severe reaction, seek professional advice. Do not use household bleach or unreviewed whitening mixtures.
Record how your skin feels over time. Notes are stored locally on this device; the app does not infer improvement from notes or photos.
Add a short note above to start a private timeline.

A small educational catalogue. Learn about common skincare ingredients and their limitations; this is not a product endorsement.
A humectant used in many moisturizers to help attract and hold water in the outer skin layer.
Caution: product formulation matters; choose a suitable finished product rather than applying concentrated raw ingredients.
Skin-identical lipids used in moisturizers to support the skin barrier and reduce moisture loss.
Caution: products vary; fragrance or other ingredients may still irritate some people.
A form of vitamin B3 used in some cosmetic products for barrier support and appearance-related benefits.
Caution: higher concentrations are not automatically better; stop use if irritation occurs.
Added to scent a product and may be listed under several names depending on the label.
Caution: fragrance can trigger irritation or allergy in some people; fragrance-free may be preferable for sensitive skin.
Kitchen lemon juice is not a tested skincare treatment and can irritate skin.
Avoid applying lemon juice to skin, especially before sunlight. It is not a safe DIY whitening method.
A finished sunscreen labelled broad-spectrum helps protect against UVA and UVB when used as directed.
Caution: use enough and reapply as directed on the label; shade and clothing also help. Availability and prices are not verified here.
